Patient: "I had it a similar sort of thing about a month ago" and when asked: "How long did that episode last for?" she replies: "Probably only about five, ten minutes."

Patient: "I've had premature ovarian failure and I've taken hrt." This supports current use/history of hormone replacement therapy.
Doctor: "Do you have any allergies at all?" Patient: "No." This supports no known allergies.
Doctor: "Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past. Past couple of weeks?" Patient: "No... No cold, cough, nothing?" Patient: "No, I've been pretty healthy."
Doctor: "Do you have a temperature at all?" Patient: "I don't think so." This supports absence of reported fever.
Doctor: "Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge, anything like that?" Patient: "No, nothing." This includes no ear pain.
Same question-answer: "Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge, anything like that?" Patient: "No, nothing." This includes no ear discharge.
Doctor: "Have you been physically sick?" Patient: "No, but I am feeling very sick." This supports no vomiting.
Doctor: "So there's no weakness of your arms and legs?" (implied query) and patient earlier: "my legs and arms and everything are working fine." This supports no limb weakness.

The transcript contains only history and advice; there is no description of any physical examination being performed during the consultation. This supports that no physical exam was done in this encounter.

Doctor: "the most common... diagnosis... is something called labyrinthitis" with 2 hours of continuous dizziness, unsteady walking, ear buzzing, and nausea. Patient denies limb weakness and has only buzzing but can hear everything: "otherwise I can hear everything," supporting no hearing loss or neurological deficit as part of the assessment.

Doctor: "I'll send the prescription across to your pharmacy... It's called semitol. Yep. It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about 10 days worth..." and confirms pharmacy: "It looks like it's the Lloyd Pharmacy on our system. Is that correct?" Patient: "Yeah."

Doctor: "I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears... While you're with the doctors, we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how you're walking, and everything." This describes arranging in-person otoscopy, BP, and gait assessment.

Doctor: "if you develop any weakness of your legs or arms or, you know, a sudden headache, any of those symptoms, or you start being violently sick with it, then, you know, you would need to take yourself to A and E." This is safety-net advice to attend the emergency department for those symptoms.

Doctor: "While you are waiting on seeing the doctor..." and later: "Just make sure you call support to book that appointment. Okay?" This indicates a follow-up (in-person) appointment is to be booked.
